speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed history; given your recent sexually active lifestyle and the history of a self-resolving monoarticular joint swelling, are you currently experiencing fever or chills? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, and Blood Cultures.

speaker: Patient
text: Experiences anxiety; denies recent flu-like symptoms, denies any known sexually transmitted infections. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That diagnosis of Multiple Sclerosis is incorrect given your symptoms; the combination of knee swelling, urinary pain, and a prior ankle attack strongly suggests a reactive arthritis rather than an autoimmune demyelinating disease. I need to see the joint and check for signs of infection, so please let me examine your right knee now. REQUEST IMAGES: Knee_X-Ray, X-Ray_Left_Ankle.

speaker: Patient
text: Experiences anxiety; denies recent flu-like symptoms, denies any known sexually transmitted infections. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome). The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee and prior ankle), dysuria, and risk factors for untreated chlamydia infection is classic for this condition, making the previous Multiple Sclerosis diagnosis incorrect.
